audit.appendOnlyBody: The database refuses UPDATE and DELETE on this table through a trigger, so an event cannot be altered or removed after the fact — including by Velnox itself.
audit.subtitle: Every authentication and authorisation event, oldest kept, newest first.

auth.apiUnreachableBody: The interface is running but the API did not answer. Signing in will not work until it does.
auth.mfaPrompt: Enter the code from your authenticator app
auth.mfaRecommended: Multi-factor authentication is strongly recommended for accounts that can manage infrastructure.
auth.mfaRecommendedNotice: Two-factor authentication is optional here. Turning it on for accounts that can manage infrastructure is the single largest improvement available to this installation.

dashboard.phaseNoticeBody: Authentication, the setup wizard, roles and optional two-factor authentication work. Proxmox inventory arrives in phase 4 and the job system in phase 5. Counters below stay at zero until there is something real to count — they are not placeholders for hidden data.
dashboard.phaseNoticeTitle: This installation is running a phase 2 build
dashboard.subtitle: Fleet overview
dashboard.title: Dashboard

docs.appliesToVersion: This Documentation applies to version V{version}
docs.availableOfflineBody: These pages are part of the build and need no internet connection. They are rebuilt from the repository every time the version changes.
docs.notTranslatedBody: This document has no translation in your language, so the English original is shown. English is canonical in any case.
docs.subtitle: The full documentation set, bundled into this installation.
docs.versionMismatchBody: This documentation was built for V{docs}, but this installation reports V{running}. That normally means an upgrade replaced one container and not the other. Re-run the installer so both come from the same build.
docs.versionMismatchTitle: Documentation and software are different versions

errors.validation: Some of the values submitted are not valid.

job.approvalPrompt: Review the exact changes below before approving.

mfa.disableBlockedBody: This installation requires two-factor authentication, so you will be asked to set it up again at your next sign-in.
mfa.disableCodeHint: Confirm with a current code from your authenticator app.

mfa.enrolUnavailableBody: The server did not return a setup code. Try again in a moment.
mfa.recoveryAcknowledge: I have saved these codes somewhere safe.

mfa.recoveryWarning: They cannot be shown again. Store them somewhere you can reach without this account.

mfa.sectionDescription: A code from an authenticator app, in addition to your password.

roles.editingPendingBody: Custom roles and per-role permission editing arrive in a later phase. The roles above are read from the API and are what the guard actually enforces.
roles.subtitle: What each role grants, read from this installation.
roles.systemRolesBody: Created at setup from a frozen catalogue of {count} permissions. A permission that is not in the catalogue does not exist — adding one is a code change, never a data-entry surface.
roles.unknownTitle: Stored permissions this build does not recognise

security.subtitle: Settings that apply to your own account.

selftest.description: Submits a job to the queue and waits for the worker to execute it. This proves the API, Redis and worker are connected — it does not touch any managed infrastructure.
selftest.disabled: Diagnostic endpoints are disabled on this installation.
selftest.title: Queue self-test

setup.masterKeyWarning: Store a backup of MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY now. Without it, every credential this installation stores becomes permanently unreadable.
setup.name: Full name
setup.organisationNameHint: Your own company. Customers are added later as tenants.
setup.passwordHint: At least {min} characters. Length matters more than symbols.
setup.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
setup.passwordWeak: This password does not meet the minimum strength requirement.
setup.subtitle: Create the first administrator account. This can only be done once.
setup.title: Set up {product}

sso.allowedDomainsHint: Comma separated. Leave empty to allow any domain the directory authenticates.
sso.breakGlassBody: Configuring a directory never disables signing in with an email address and password. A directory outage must not lock you out of the tool you would use to investigate it.
sso.cardDescription: Read from the directory at sign-in. Velnox stores no directory passwords.
sso.clientSecretHint: Stored encrypted. It is never shown again after saving.
sso.clientSecretStored: A secret is stored. Leave blank to keep it, or enter a new one to replace it.
sso.discoveryUrlHint: The OpenID configuration endpoint for your tenant. Must be HTTPS and publicly resolvable.
sso.notAvailableBody: This build can hold and check the configuration. Signing in through Entra ID arrives in a later phase, so the button is not shown on the sign-in page yet.
sso.subtitle: Sign in with a Microsoft Entra ID directory.
sso.testOk: The provider answered and the discovery document is valid.

identifiers.body: The Overview page of your new app registration shows both. Paste them here.
identifiers.clientHint: Also on the Overview page. Not the object ID.
identifiers.derived: Velnox will use this discovery document, built from the tenant ID:
identifiers.tenantHint: A GUID on the Overview page of the app registration.
identifiers.title: Copy the two identifiers back

intro.body: Connecting a directory means switching between this page and the Microsoft Entra admin center a few times. Here is what you will need.
intro.need1: Access to the Microsoft Entra admin center at entra.microsoft.com.
intro.need2: Permission to create an app registration — Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator or Global Administrator.
intro.need3: A few minutes without interruption: a client secret is shown only once, immediately after you create it.
intro.title: Before you start

register.accountTypes: For account types, choose "Accounts in this organizational directory only" unless you deliberately want guests from other tenants to sign in.
register.body: In the Entra admin center go to Identity → Applications → App registrations, and choose New registration. Use these two values.
register.redirectHint: Add it under platform "Web". It must match exactly — a trailing slash is a different URI to Entra.
register.title: Create the app registration

restrict.body: Optional. Limiting the email domains that may sign in is worth doing if your directory contains guest accounts.
restrict.title: Restrict who may sign in

secret.alreadyStored: A secret is already stored. Leave this blank to keep it, or paste a new one to replace it.
secret.body: In the app registration go to Certificates & secrets → Client secrets → New client secret. Copy the Value, not the Secret ID.
secret.hint: Entra shows the value once. If you navigate away before copying it, delete the secret and create another.
secret.title: Create a client secret

test.body: Velnox will store the configuration and ask the provider for its discovery document, so you find out now rather than at the first sign-in.
test.secretEntered: A new secret will be stored
test.secretMissing: None — the connection will not work without one
test.title: Save and check the connection

system.subtitle: Live readiness of this installation
system.title: Service status
system.workerHint: The worker has no network port by design; its liveness is reported through a heartbeat.

users.createBody: Velnox sends no email, so there is no invitation. Set an initial password and pass it on yourself; the new account can change it after signing in.
users.disabledNotice: This account is disabled. Its sessions were revoked and it cannot sign in.
users.foundingBody: This is the account the setup wizard created, and the way back into a misconfigured installation. Its roles cannot be taken away by anyone, including itself. Another administrator can disable it — but not while no other enabled account can administer this installation.
users.initialPasswordHint: At least {min} characters, held to the same rule as every other password.
users.managementPendingBody: Inviting users, assigning roles and deactivating accounts arrive with the roles interface. The accounts above are read from the API.
users.mfaGapTitle: {count, plural, one {# privileged account without a second factor} other {# privileged accounts without a second factor}}
users.noRoles: No roles — this account can sign in but do nothing.
users.subtitle: Accounts that can sign in to this installation.
